findings:
🔴 [D2-rcpt-verdict-claim] MUST-FIX — check-phase-review-receipt.js Mode A trusts `receipt.verdict` (and `open_findings`) as bare claims: it validates only chain contiguity, range.json base/head, recomputed diff_sha256, and branch head, and never reads the review evidence (findings.json / dispositions) whose location it even records per chain entry (`dispositions_path`). Concrete failure: an implementer can hand-write `receipt-<phase>.json` with verdict SHIP-AS-IS and open_findings [] plus `review-<phase>/g1/range.json` whose diff_sha256 they recompute with `git diff | sha256sum`, and the gate exits 0 with no review having occurred — a direct violation of the stated ADR-0001 constraint (verdicts re-derived from artifacts, never trusted from a claim) and an affirmative answer to the spec's "can an implementer forge a passing receipt?". Smallest remediation: in Mode A, for each chain generation re-run finalize's union-on-verified-critical aggregation over `review-<phase>/g<gen>/findings.json` and that generation's dispositions (canonicalized to a ledger-relative path rather than the trusted absolute `dispositions_path`), and exit 1 if any verified Critical exists or the recomputed verdict contradicts `receipt.verdict`.
🟠 [D2-rcpt-base-unanchored] MUST-FIX — the "rooted at the phase base" rule is self-referential: chain[0].base is compared only to `receipt.phase_base_sha`, which comes from the same writable receipt, and the checker accepts no externally supplied phase base. Concrete failure: combined with the verdict-claim gap, a forger sets base = head = current branch head (empty diff, trivially matching sha256) and the fabricated receipt passes; even absent malice, nothing binds the chain to where the phase actually started. Smallest remediation: require the expected phase base from the caller (e.g., a mandatory `--phase-base <sha>` flag, or derive it from the phase-start marker/merge-base under `--repo-root`) and reject unless chain[0].base equals it.
🟡 [D2-checker-diff-maxbuffer] MUST-FIX — the checker's `spawnSync('git', ['diff', base, head])` uses Node's default 1 MB maxBuffer while collect's runGitDiff sets 64 MB: any generation whose diff exceeds 1 MB yields `diffRes.status === null` and the gate exits 1 for a perfectly valid receipt, permanently blocking the phase (fail-closed availability break of the gate itself). Smallest remediation: add `maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024` to this spawnSync to match collect.
🟡 [D2-chain-dup-poison] MUST-FIX — re-running collect for the same generation (the natural retry after a head-movement abort, which appends a head-less `{generation, base, status:'aborted'}` entry) appends a second entry for that generation; finalize's `chain.find(c => c.generation === generation)` then flips the FIRST (aborted, head-undefined) entry to 'finalized' while the real pending entry stays pending, and the checker's `generation === i+1` / range-head rules reject the resulting receipt — the phase becomes unpassable without hand-editing chain.json. Smallest remediation: have finalize select the last entry for the generation (`chain.filter(...).pop()`) and have collect drop prior non-finalized same-generation entries before appending.
🔵 [D2-optout-regex-class] CUT/FOLLOW-UP — in handleOptOut the character class `[\s#*->]` parses `*->` as a range (matching + , . / digits : ; < = too), so a line like "9plan_review: off" can set configured_value; excluded from this version because Mode A re-derives the off value from the resolver and the config sha256, so no gate decision depends on the loosened parse — tighten when the knob parser is next touched.
🔵 [D2-no-e2e-receipt-test] CUT/FOLLOW-UP — no test feeds a real collect→finalize receipt through check-phase-review-receipt (the finalize-test receipts use fake shas like "base111" and are never checker-validated), so writer/checker format drift would ship silently; excluded from this version because each script's own contract tests do bind its behavior (a gutted gate fails checker-test cases 3/4/5/6/8/9/10, so the deleted-gate concern is covered) — add one E2E case in D3.
🔵 [D2-stub-seat-id-leak] CUT/FOLLOW-UP — production runSeatDispatch exports a STUB_SEAT_ID test seam into dispatch-review.sh's environment; harmless today (the real script ignores it) and removing it would require reworking the seat-stub mechanism, so it is excluded as cosmetic hardening.
